faq.q: What is the friction coefficient of your PTFE release film, and does it enable use as a sliding or bearing surface?
faq.a: PTFE has one of the lowest friction coefficients of any solid material (μ = 0.04–0.10, static and dynamic). This means our PTFE films function not only as release layers but also as low-friction bearing films, slide pads, and wear surfaces in mechanical assemblies. Applications include bridge expansion joints, architectural sliding joints, and machinery bearing surfaces.

faq.q: Do you offer any transparent or optically clear high-temperature release films?
faq.a: Yes, our PTFE films (MR1/2 series in natural/translucent) and ETFE-based films offer high optical clarity — ETFE transmits over 90% of visible light. For 应用行业页 requiring visual inspection through the release layer during processing (e.g., composite lay-up, adhesive bond inspection), our ETFE-EC film (white, slightly translucent) or thin PTFE films are recommended.

faq.q: What is the maximum roll width available for your PTFE release film without adhesive (bare film)?
faq.a: Our bare PTFE film is available in standard widths up to 1,220mm (MR1/2 series) and up to 1,270mm (VB-3 series). For 应用行业页 requiring widths beyond these, we can explore custom production or joining of strips. The maximum width is determined by our casting line width. Contact our technical team for wider-format requirements.

faq.q: Can your PTFE tape be used to mask and protect surfaces during anodizing, electroplating, or 化工 etching?
faq.a: Yes, PTFE tape is excellent for masking in surface treatment processes. It is resistant to the acids, alkalis, and plating bath 化工s used in anodizing (sulfuric, chromic, phosphoric acids), electroplating baths, and 化工 etching processes. It leaves no adhesive residue and maintains its masking performance in both acidic and alkaline bath environments.

faq.q: What is the dielectric strength of your PTFE release film for electrical insulation 应用行业页?
faq.a: Our PTFE film has a dielectric strength exceeding 50kV/mm at 25μm thickness, and dielectric constant of 2.1 (stable across all frequencies and temperatures). Volume resistivity exceeds 10¹⁸ Ω·cm. These outstanding electrical properties make PTFE the preferred insulation material for high-frequency circuits, transformers, and high-voltage 应用行业页.

faq.q: Can I use your release film in a continuous belt furnace or conveyor oven process?
faq.a: Our PTFE films can be fabricated into continuous belts for conveyor oven 应用行业页 in 电子 (reflow soldering, conformal coating cure), food processing, and industrial curing lines. Belt widths up to 1,220mm and any length can be supplied. Custom joining (seaming) methods are available. The belts can run at speeds of several meters per minute at temperatures up to 260°C.

faq.q: What is the thermal shrinkage of your high-temperature release film, and how does it affect dimensional accuracy in composite parts?
faq.a: PTFE has very low thermal shrinkage (<1% in both directions at 200°C), ensuring dimensional stability during high-temperature processing. ETFE-EC shows ≤5°C thermal shrinkage specification. Minimal shrinkage is critical in precision composite manufacturing where dimensional tolerances are tight. We provide shrinkage data across the operating temperature range upon request.

faq.q: How does your release film compare to PFA film for high-temperature release 应用行业页?
faq.a: PTFE offers the highest continuous service temperature of all our films (260°C) and the lowest surface energy, making it the best release performance. PFA provides similar 化工 resistance and slightly better flow in melt-processed forms. For release film 应用行业页, PTFE is generally preferred. PFA film excels in thermoforming 应用行业页 where complex shapes are required.

faq.q: Can your release film be used in battery manufacturing processes, such as lithium-ion electrode coating?
faq.a: Yes, our PTFE and ETFE release films are used in lithium-ion battery manufacturing: as release substrates during electrode slurry coating and drying, as separator films during calendering, and as peel-off layers for transfer coating processes. They are 化工ly resistant to battery electrolytes (NMP, DMF, ethylene carbonate) and stable at electrode drying temperatures (120–180°C).

faq.q: How does humidity and moisture affect the performance of your high-temperature release film?
faq.a: PTFE is inherently hydrophobic with a water absorption rate near zero (<0.01%), making it unaffected by humidity or moisture exposure. Unlike polyimide or other high-temp films, PTFE does not absorb moisture that could vaporize during heating (causing blistering). This makes our PTFE films particularly reliable in tropical or humid manufacturing environments.

faq.q: What are the regulatory compliances for your release films used in food and pharmaceutical packaging?
faq.a: Our PTFE-based films comply with: FDA 21 CFR 177.1550 (PTFE resins for food contact), EU Regulation 10/2011 (food contact plastics), and are free from substances of concern under REACH and RoHS regulations. For pharmaceutical 应用行业页, materials comply with USP Class VI and ISO 10993 biocompatibility standards. Full regulatory documentation packages are available.

faq.q: Can your PTFE film be used in heat press and sublimation printing 应用行业页?
faq.a: Absolutely — PTFE sheets are a staple in heat press and sublimation printing. They protect the heat platen from sublimation ink transfer, protect garments from direct heat contact, and prevent ghosting. Our PTFE films at 100–160μm thickness are the ideal range for this application. They can be used repeatedly across hundreds of heat press cycles.

faq.q: Is your high-temperature release film compatible with silicone rubber molding and RTV processes?
faq.a: Yes, PTFE release films are excellent release layers for silicone rubber molding. PTFE's low surface energy means even silicone (itself a release agent for many materials) does not adhere. This is crucial for RTV molding where the part would otherwise stick to silicone tooling. We recommend our HSM 22S or HM 32S grades for silicone molding 应用行业页.

faq.q: What are the standard roll widths for your PTFE tape, and can you supply custom slit widths?
faq.a: Our PTFE tapes are available in standard widths ranging from 6mm to the full film width (up to 1,220mm for PTFE). Custom slit widths can be supplied in increments as small as 1mm, subject to minimum order quantities. Common narrow slit widths (12mm, 25mm, 50mm, 100mm) are typically in stock for fast delivery.

faq.q: How do I properly apply and remove PTFE release tape without leaving residue?
faq.a: For optimal application: ensure the surface is clean, dry, and free of oils; apply at room temperature with moderate pressure; smooth out air bubbles. For removal: allow the substrate to cool to below 100°C before peeling; peel at a low angle (15–30°) against the direction of application. If residue occurs, clean with IPA solvent. Avoid removal at peak operating temperature.

faq.q: Can your PTFE tape withstand the temperatures used in powder coating ovens (160–220°C)?
faq.a: Yes, our PTFE tapes are specifically suitable for powder coating masking 应用行业页. They withstand typical powder coating cure temperatures (160–220°C) without delaminating, burning, or leaving adhesive residue. They are easy to remove after cooling and leave clean, sharp masking lines. Used for protecting threads, bearings, and precision surfaces from powder coating overspray.

faq.q: What is the surface roughness of your PTFE release film, and does it affect the surface finish of molded parts?
faq.a: Our PTFE films have a very smooth surface (Ra <0.1μm for standard glossy grades). The film surface directly transfers its finish to the composite or molded part during curing — glossy PTFE produces glossy parts, textured PTFE produces matte or patterned surfaces. We can supply custom surface finishes (gloss, matte, micro-textured) depending on your aesthetic or functional requirements.

faq.q: Is your PTFE film non-toxic and safe for use in 医药 device manufacturing?
faq.a: PTFE is biologically inert, non-toxic, and FDA-approved for 医药 use. Our PTFE films contain no plasticizers, fillers, or additives that could leach. They are used in 医药 device manufacturing as release layers in molding, as packaging films, and in catheter and implant production. ISO biocompatibility testing documentation is available upon request.

faq.q: Does your PTFE release film work at cryogenic temperatures for LNG or 航空 应用行业页?
faq.a: Yes, PTFE remains flexible and functional at cryogenic temperatures down to -200°C (liquid nitrogen temperature). Unlike most polymers that become brittle, PTFE retains its structural integrity and 化工 resistance at cryogenic conditions. This makes our PTFE films suitable for LNG tank sealing, cryogenic valve packing, and 航空 应用行业页 involving liquid propellants.

faq.q: What are the differences between your orange (HSM 22S), gray (HSM 22S), and rust-red (HM 32S/52S) PTFE tape 产品页?
faq.a: The color differences reflect different backing film thicknesses and adhesive thicknesses: Orange HSM 22S (100μm = 50μm film + 50μm adhesive) offers maximum conformability. Gray HSM 22S (80μm = 50μm film + 30μm adhesive) is thinner with less adhesive. HM 32S (110μm) and HM 52S (160μm) use thicker film for longer service life. Choose based on conformability needs vs. durability requirements.

faq.q: Can your high-temperature film be used as a vacuum bagging film in composite manufacturing?
faq.a: Our ETFE-based films can serve as vacuum bagging components due to their excellent gas barrier properties and heat resistance up to 165°C (ETFE-EC) or 260°C (PTFE). For standard epoxy prepreg curing (120–180°C), our films are compatible. For PEEK and high-performance thermoplastic composites requiring >200°C, the PTFE grade is recommended.

faq.q: What is the 化工 resistance of your high-temperature release film to solvents used in 电子 manufacturing?
faq.a: Our PTFE-based films resist virtually all solvents used in 电子: isopropyl alcohol (IPA), acetone, MEK, toluene, flux activators, and conformal coating solvents. PTFE's 化工 resistance is among the highest of any polymer. Our ETFE-EC variant also offers good solvent resistance, with specific compatibility data available.

faq.q: What is the peel adhesion strength of your PTFE release tape, and how does it compare across surfaces?
faq.a: The silicone PSA on our PTFE tapes provides moderate-high initial tack, sufficient for secure positioning during assembly. Specific peel strength values are available per product grade. Adhesion to stainless steel is typically higher than to PTFE or ceramic surfaces. Elevated temperature reduces effective peel strength slightly — data at 25°C and 180°C available on request.

faq.q: How many times can your release film be reused before it needs to be replaced?
faq.a: Reuse cycles depend heavily on operating temperature, pressure, and the surface being released from. Under typical press curing conditions (180°C, 5 bar), our PTFE films typically last 10–50 cycles. In lighter 应用行业页 such as heat sealing jaws (160°C), service life can extend to hundreds of cycles. We recommend testing under your specific conditions for precise cycle count data.

faq.q: Is your release film suitable for use in PCB and 电子 assembly processes?
faq.a: Our PTFE and PET release tapes are widely used in PCB manufacturing: as masking tape during wave soldering , as a carrier film for SMT pick-and-place processes, and as a separator in stack-press lamination of multilayer PCBs. They withstand lead-free solder temperatures (260–280°C).

faq.q: Can your high-temperature release film be used in autoclave composite manufacturing?
faq.a: Yes, our PTFE release films are widely used in autoclave composite manufacturing. They function as peel-ply or release layer between the part and tooling/vacuum bag. The film releases cleanly after curing at temperatures up to 260°C and pressures up to 10 bar (typical autoclave conditions). It leaves no residue on carbon fiber or glass fiber parts.

faq.q: What industries most commonly use your high-temperature release film, and why?
faq.a: Key industries include: 电子 manufacturing (wave soldering, conformal coating masking), composite manufacturing (autoclave and press curing), food processing equipment (non-stick conveyor belts and baking molds), packaging (heat sealing jaws), and 航空 (pre-preg lay-up and vacuum bagging). In all cases, the film must survive process temperatures while releasing cleanly without contaminating the product.

faq.q: What types of adhesive are used in your release film tapes, and what are the bonding differences?
faq.a: Our PTFE tapes use silicone pressure-sensitive adhesive (PSA), which maintains adhesion and release properties across the full temperature range (-70°C to +260°C). Our ETFE-EC tape uses acrylic PSA, which is preferred for moderate temperature 应用行业页 (up to 165°C) where longer-term bonding strength is more important than ultra-high-temp performance.

faq.q: What thicknesses are available for your PTFE release films, and how do I choose the right one?
faq.a: We offer four main PTFE tape configurations: HSM 22S (100μm or 80μm), HM 32S (110μm), and HM 52S (160μm). Thinner films (80–100μm) are used where conformability and close contact are needed; thicker films (110–160μm) offer longer service life in repeated-use press operations. We recommend discussing your cycle counts and pressure parameters.

faq.q: What is the maximum continuous operating temperature of your high-temperature release film?
faq.a: Our PTFE-based release films withstand continuous operation at +260°C (500°F) and can tolerate short-term peaks up to +280°C. ETFE-EC variants operate continuously at -150°C to +165°C. PET-based variants have a maximum of 204°C. The choice depends on your process requirements.

faq.q: What is a high-temperature release film and what materials are typically used in your product?
faq.a: A high-temperature release film is a specialty film coated with release agents (typically silicone or fluoropolymer) that prevents adhesion at elevated temperatures. Our product line uses PTFE (Teflon) film as the primary substrate, offering release properties from -70°C to +260°C. We also offer ETFE-EC variants with acrylic adhesive for specific bonding 应用行业页.

faq.q: How does ETFE compare to FEP film for wire and cable insulation 应用行业页?
faq.a: ETFE has higher tensile strength (48MPa vs. FEP's ~24MPa) and better abrasion resistance, making it preferred for wire and cable jacketing in 航空 and military 应用行业页 where mechanical durability is critical. FEP offers slightly better 化工 resistance and lower friction. ETFE is preferred where mechanical toughness matters most.

faq.q: What is the anti-static or ESD performance of ETFE in 电子 manufacturing environments?
faq.a: Standard ETFE is an excellent electrical insulator (surface resistivity >10¹⁶ Ω/sq), which can present ESD risks in 电子 manufacturing. We offer antistatic-treated or carbon-loaded ETFE grades with surface resistivity in the 10⁶–10⁹ Ω/sq range, suitable for ESD-sensitive assembly lines and component packaging.

faq.q: Can ETFE film withstand 化工 exposure common in 半导体 fabs (HF, sulfuric acid, solvents)?
faq.a: ETFE demonstrates excellent resistance to hydrofluoric acid (HF), sulfuric acid, nitric acid, and most organic solvents — substances that attack many other plastics and metals. It is widely used in 半导体 wet processing equipment, 化工 handling lines, and cleanroom 应用行业页. Chemical compatibility charts are available.

faq.q: What is the dielectric constant of ETFE, and is it suitable for high-frequency PCB 应用行业页?
faq.a: ETFE has a dielectric constant of approximately 2.6–2.8 at 1MHz and remains stable across a wide frequency range. This low, stable dielectric constant makes ETFE suitable for high-frequency microwave PCB substrates, antenna insulation layers, and radar equipment. We can provide dielectric property data sheets for design engineers.

faq.q: Do you supply ETFE in roll or sheet format, and what are the standard roll lengths?
faq.a: ETFE is available in roll format as standard. Roll lengths depend on thickness and width — typically 100–500 linear meters per roll, with each roll weighing approximately 10–15kg. Sheet cutting is available for custom dimensions. We can discuss specific roll configurations based on your processing needs.

faq.q: Can ETFE film be used for flexible 电子 and wearable device substrates?
faq.a: ETFE is gaining attention in flexible 电子 due to its electrical insulation, flexibility, and 化工 resistance. It is used as a substrate for flexible circuits and piezoelectric sensors, and as encapsulation for wearable 电子. Its biocompatibility also makes it suitable for 医药 wearables. Custom thin gauges (down to 12μm) are available.

faq.q: How does ETFE's thermal insulation compare to glass in 建材 envelopes?
faq.a: Single-layer ETFE has a U-value similar to single-pane glass (~5.7 W/m²K). However, multi-layer ETFE cushion systems with trapped air layers achieve U-values of 1.5–2.0 W/m²K, comparable to double-pane low-E glass. Four-layer cushions can achieve U-values below 1.0 W/m²K, offering excellent thermal performance.

faq.q: What is the expected weathering lifespan of your ETFE film under outdoor UV exposure?
faq.a: Our ETFE film maintains its optical and mechanical properties for over 25 years of outdoor exposure. We conduct accelerated weathering tests equivalent to 30+ years using xenon arc chambers. ETFE does not yellow, crack, or delaminate under prolonged UV exposure. Long-term performance data is available upon request.

faq.q: Can perforated ETFE film be supplied, and what are the typical 应用行业页?
faq.a: Yes, we offer ETFE with custom perforation patterns. Perforated ETFE is used in acoustic panels (sound absorption while maintaining transparency), ventilated façades, air distribution systems in greenhouses, and filtration media. Hole size, pitch, and pattern can be customized to meet airflow or acoustic requirements.

faq.q: What quality inspection processes do you use for ETFE film production?
faq.a: Every production run undergoes online defect detection using optical inspection systems, thickness measurement with in-line gauges, and melt flow index testing. Pre-shipment checks include tensile strength, elongation, transmittance, and surface energy tests. We maintain full batch traceability and provide CoA (Certificate of Analysis) with every shipment.

faq.q: Can ETFE film be printed with solar cell patterns for BIPV (Building Integrated Photovoltaics)?
faq.a: Yes, ETFE is an ideal substrate for BIPV 应用行业页. It can receive screen-printed, inkjet-printed, or sputtered photovoltaic cell patterns and conductive inks. Its transparency allows for semi-transparent BIPV panels that double as architectural glazing. We can supply treated ETFE ready for PV processing.

faq.q: How does ETFE film behave in fire, and what fire ratings does it achieve?
faq.a: ETFE is inherently flame-retardant without additives — it has a limiting oxygen index (LOI) above 30%, meaning it does not sustain combustion in normal air. Upon ignition, it self-extinguishes and does not drip burning material. It meets UL94 V-0 rating and satisfies European fire class B-s1,d0 requirements for many 建材 应用行业页.

faq.q: What certifications does your ETFE film hold (UL, RoHS, REACH, etc.)?
faq.a: Our ETFE film holds UL certification and passes HF (halogen-free flame) and SGS testing. Products are RoHS compliant and meet REACH SVHC substance requirements. Additional certifications such as IATF 16949 (automotive) and AS9100 (航空) are available for specific product lines.

faq.q: Does your ETFE film meet food contact and pharmaceutical purity standards?
faq.a: Our ETFE film is produced without plasticizers or additives, making it compliant with FDA 21 CFR regulations for food contact and suitable for pharmaceutical 应用行业页. It has excellent 化工 inertness and will not leach compounds into food or drug 产品页. Documentation for compliance is available upon request.

faq.q: Can ETFE film be laminated with other materials for composite 应用行业页?
faq.a: Yes, ETFE can be laminated with metals (aluminum, copper), textiles, foams, and other films. Surface treatment (plasma or 化工 etching) is required first to enhance adhesion. We supply ETFE pre-treated and ready for lamination, and can collaborate on composite development projects.

faq.q: What is the minimum order quantity for ETFE film, and what is the typical lead time?
faq.a: Minimum order quantities vary by specification. Standard 产品页 (common thicknesses and widths) typically have an MOQ of 100kg. Custom specifications may require higher minimums. Standard lead time is 2–4 weeks; custom orders may require 4–8 weeks. Please contact our sales team for specific quotations.

faq.q: Is ETFE recyclable, and what is its environmental footprint compared to glass?
faq.a: ETFE is fully recyclable — it can be melted down and reprocessed into new film. Its production energy is significantly lower than glass per unit area (ETFE weighs ~350g/m² vs. 25kg/m² for glass). The longevity of ETFE further reduces lifecycle environmental impact. We are aligned with circular economy principles.

faq.q: How does ETFE perform in 航空 and satellite 应用行业页?
faq.a: ETFE's resistance to radiation, extreme temperature cycling (-70°C to +150°C), and vacuum conditions make it highly suitable for 航空 wiring insulation, flexible solar array substrates, and thermal blankets. It holds AS9100 certification eligibility and passes outgassing tests per ASTM E595 standard.

faq.q: What is the self-cleaning mechanism of ETFE, and does it require any maintenance?
faq.a: ETFE has an extremely low surface energy (~31 mN/m), which causes water to bead and roll off, carrying dust particles away. Rain is typically sufficient to keep ETFE surfaces clean. In heavily polluted urban environments, occasional washing with water is recommended. No 化工 cleaners are needed.

faq.q: What is the tensile strength and elongation of your ETFE film, and how does it handle wind loading?
faq.a: Our ETFE has a tensile strength of 48 MPa and elongation at break of 300%. For wind loading in architectural 应用行业页, ETFE cushion systems are designed to be pre-stressed — the pneumatic inflation pressure is adjusted so the film carries loads through tension rather than bending. Engineering support for load calculations is available.

faq.q: Can ETFE film be used for agricultural greenhouse covering, and what are its advantages over PE film?
faq.a: ETFE is an excellent greenhouse material. It outperforms standard PE film in several ways: lifespan exceeds 20 years (vs. 1–3 years for PE), it maintains transmittance without yellowing, is 化工ly resistant to pesticides and fertilizers, and is fully recyclable. While the upfront cost is higher, the long-term ROI is significantly superior.

faq.q: What color options are available for ETFE film, and are printed patterns possible?
faq.a: We offer ETFE in transparent, white, frosted (matte), red, blue, and with dot-pattern (frit) printing. Custom colors and printed patterns — including branding, gradients, and decorative motifs — are available for architectural and design 应用行业页. Minimum order quantities apply for custom prints.

faq.q: How does ETFE compare to PVDF film for use as a solar panel front sheet?
faq.a: ETFE offers higher light transmittance (>90% vs. ~88% for PVDF), greater flexibility, and superior weathering resistance over 25+ years. PVDF is more cost-effective and easier to thermoform. For high-efficiency flexible modules, ETFE is preferred; for conventional rigid panels requiring easy processing, PVDF is often chosen.

faq.q: Is your ETFE film certified for use in photovoltaic solar panels, and what are the relevant standards?
faq.a: Our ETFE film meets key PV industry requirements including IEC 61215, IEC 61730, and UL certifications. It passes PCT accelerated aging tests and damp-heat tests (85°C/85% RH for 1,000 hours). ETFE is widely used as front-sheet material for flexible and bifacial solar modules.

faq.q: What surface treatments do you offer for ETFE, and when is plasma or 化工 etching recommended?
faq.a: We offer plasma treatment and 化工 etching (sodium etching) for ETFE. Plasma treatment is recommended for bonding, printing, or lamination 应用行业页. Chemical etching creates a micro-rough surface that significantly enhances adhesion — ideal for structural composites or when applying pressure-sensitive adhesives.

faq.q: Can ETFE film be heat-welded on-site, and what equipment is required?
faq.a: Yes, ETFE is fully heat-weldable using standard hot-air welding or wedge-welding machines. No special solvents are required. Our technical team can provide welding parameter guidelines (temperature range 250–280°C, speed settings) and on-request training support for fabricators.

faq.q: How does ETFE perform in extreme cold climates, such as Nordic countries or Canada?
faq.a: ETFE retains excellent flexibility and mechanical strength at temperatures as low as -70°C, making it suitable for Arctic and sub-Arctic climates. Its elongation at break remains at 300%, preventing cracking. The material does not become brittle in freezing conditions, unlike many alternatives.

faq.q: What is the certified light transmittance of your ETFE film, and does it affect UV filtration?
faq.a: Our ETFE film achieves over 92% light transmittance (HP/AG grades). ETFE naturally blocks short-wave UV below 200nm; mid-range UV (280–380nm) is partly transmitted. For 应用行业页 requiring controlled UV filtering — such as greenhouses or museums — we can add UV-blocking coatings or additives.

faq.q: What thicknesses and widths does your ETFE film come in, and can you customize dimensions?
faq.a: Our standard ETFE film ranges from 12µm to 500µm in thickness. Standard width reaches 1,600mm, with custom widths up to 2,100mm available. We support full customization of thickness, width, length, and color to match your project specifications.

faq.q: What is ETFE film and how does it differ from traditional glass or polycarbonate in construction?
faq.a: ETFE (Ethylene Tetrafluoroethylene) is a fluoropolymer film known for its exceptional transparency (>92%), light weight (1% of glass), and tensile strength. Unlike glass, ETFE can be formed into pneumatic cushion structures, is self-cleaning, and has a lifespan exceeding 25 years. Compared to polycarbonate, it offers superior UV resistance and does not yellow over time.

faq.q: How does ETFE compare to FEP film in terms of weight?
faq.a: In specific release and technical 应用行业页, our ETFE MR (Release Grade) film is 20% lighter per unit area than FEP film, which can reduce the overall structural load of your project.

faq.q: Why is ETFE considered a "self-cleaning" material?
faq.a: Thanks to its low coefficient of friction and non-stick properties, the film exhibits a "Lotus Effect". Dust and dirt do not easily adhere to the surface and are typically washed away by natural rainfall.

faq.q: Do you offer different finishes or colors for specific agricultural needs?
faq.a: Yes. Our ETFE AG (Architectural/Agricultural Grade) series comes in transparent, matte, white, and blue. We also offer functional variants such as UV-blocking or Infrared-blocking versions to optimize the growing environment.

faq.q: Can the film be bonded to other materials or frames?
faq.a: Yes. We provide specialized surface treatments, including plasma treatment and 化工 etching, to create bondable surfaces for complex composite 应用行业页 or frame attachments.

faq.q: What thicknesses and widths are available for international orders?
faq.a: We offer a versatile range of thicknesses from 12µm to 500µm. While our standard maximum width is 2100mm, we can slit the film to any width based on specific customer requirements.

faq.q: Does the film absorb water or 化工s used in farming?
faq.a: No. Our ETFE film has an extremely low water absorption rate of <0.03% and is 化工ly inert to most 化工s and solvents used in agricultural processes.

faq.q: What are the mechanical strengths of your film regarding wind and hail resistance?
faq.a: Our film is engineered for durability. It has a tensile strength of 48 MPa and a high elongation at break of 300%. This flexibility allows it to absorb impacts from hail or withstand high wind loads without tearing.

faq.q: How does ETFE handle extreme temperatures in different climates?
faq.a: VitaFlon® ETFE offers excellent resistance to both high and low temperatures. Its long-term stable working temperature ranges from -80°C to 165°C, and it can withstand peak temperatures up to 230°C.

faq.q: What is the light transmission rate of your ETFE film for agricultural use?
faq.a: Our ETFE film provides exceptional optical clarity with a solar light transmission rate exceeding 95% (tested via ASTM E424). It maintains high transmittance (over 95%) across the ultraviolet (UV) and far-infrared spectrums.

faq.q: What is the 化工 composition of PLUSXTECH ETFE film?
faq.a: Our VitaFlon® ETFE is a melt-extruded film made from 100% ethylene-tetrafluoroethylene copolymer resin. It offers the superior properties of fluoropolymers, such as heat weldability and 化工 inertness, without any mixed plastics or additives.

faq.q: Why can ETFE film be utilized for roofing in construction?
faq.a: ETFE film is a durable and lightweight film 产品页, its weight is about 1% of the weight of the glass. 92% high light transmission can effectively use natural light, easy to make the 家装 full of light.Strong weather resistance, corrosion resistance, and flame retardant properties ensure outdoor use for approximately 30 years. The non-adhesive surface maintains a clean and beautiful appearance at all times, reducing the cost of cleaning and maintenance.

faq.q: What are the advantages of FEP film?
faq.a: FEP film has excellent weather resistance, corrosion resistance,dielectric properties and outstanding insulation properties,which is currently used in a variety of electrical insulation parts.Through the material modification upgrade and satisfying different needs of customers, PLUSXTECH enhances the corresponding product performance, expands the scope of use of FEP film in different scenarios.

faq.q: What is the difference between PLUSXTECH polymer film and other film on the market?
faq.a: PLUSXTECH has the independent R&D center, which can modify and upgrade the raw materials. The excellent production technology allows our film to be produced without adding other solvents,ensuring that the 产品页 contain high purity and the maximum energy efficiency is brought into full play in every application scenario.
